32: “Yes, but did it hurt you much?” Olénin asked once more.
30: “Let me finish. He stood a pailful, and we drank it, but the blood went on flowing. The whole room was drenched and covered with blood. Grandad Burlák, he says, ‘The lad will give up the ghost. Stand a bottle of the sweet sort, or we shall have you taken up!’ They bought more drink, and boozed and boozed—”
28: “Well, but did it hurt?” Olénin asked again, scarcely listening to the tale.
25: “Yes, and did it hurt?” asked Olénin. “Vanyúsha, will you soon be ready?” he added.
23: “Oh, just so. We were drinking. Vánka Sítkin, one of the Cossacks, got merry, and puff! he gave me one from his pistol just here.”
20: “But you’ve got a bullet in your back,” remarked Vanyúsha, who was clearing up the room. “That was the Cossacks fooling about,” answered Eróshka.
19: Olénin said nothing more, but ran out of the hut.
17: “Get away. I’m sick of you!” shouted the girl, stamping her foot, and moved threateningly towards him. And her face expressed such abhorrence, such contempt, and such anger that Olénin suddenly understood that there was no hope for him, and that his first impression of this woman’s inaccessibility had been perfectly correct.
16: “Maryánka, don’t speak like that,” Olénin entreated.
15: “Maryánka!” said Olénin, approaching her. “You will never get anything from me!”
14: “Lukáshka?” said Olénin. “Go away! What do you want?”
12: “What?” she repeated in a rough voice. “Cossacks have been killed, that’s what for.”
10: “What are you crying for? What is it?”
8: “Leave me alone!” she said. Her face did not change but the tears ran down her cheeks.
7: Olénin again said: “Maryánka, I have come—”
5: She suddenly turned. There was a scarcely perceptible trace of tears in her eyes and her face was beautiful in its sadness. She looked at him in silent dignity.
4: “Maryánka,” said he, “I say, Maryánka! May I come in?”
2: It was growing dark when Olénin returned, and he could not collect himself after what he had seen. But towards night memories of the evening before came rushing to his mind. He looked out of the window, Maryánka was passing to and fro from the house to the cowshed, putting things straight. Her mother had gone to the vineyard and her father to the office. Olénin could not wait till she had quite finished her work, but went out to meet her. She was in the hut standing with her back towards him. Olénin thought she felt shy.
0: The bodies were brought to the village office. The women and the little boys hastened to look at them.
